title: Inquiry judge wants police to have more crisis-intervention training in wake of Edmonton shooting
subtitle: Man wounded one officer in the leg before he was shot to death by police
article: A judge recommends that police get more training to deal with vulnerable people after a fatal police shooting during an Edmonton traffic stop.
Michael Perreault had a long history of mental health and addiction problems when Edmonton police pulled him over for impaired driving in May 2015.
A fatality inquiry heard Perreault, 31, refused to get out of his car, pulled out a sawed-off shotgun and wounded one officer in the leg.
He then aimed his gun at a second officer, who shot him in the head.
The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team determined the shooting was justified and the officer would not face charges.

Provincial court Judge Jody Moher recommended in a report that Alberta police get crisis intervention and de-escalation training to help them deal with people with mental health and addictions issues.
She also asked that police review recommendations, including a "zero-death goal," that stemmed from the fatal shooting of Sammy Yatim in Toronto in 2013.
Another report to be released later this year about 10 fatal police shootings in Calgary in 2016 is also recommended reading, Moher said.
She further suggested there be ongoing vigilance, monitoring and education for heath-care workers regarding the misuse of opioid pain medication.
"Michael David Perreault was a man in crisis, with a long history of mental health issues exacerbated or precipitated by both prescription and illegal drug abuse," Moher wrote.

Perreault's father told the inquiry he believed doctors contributed to his son's addiction. Records showed that in the year before his death Perreault saw physicians more than 55 times. He had a long history of pain complaints related to vehicle crashes and work injuries.
More than one doctor refused to see Perreault or refill prescriptions for opiates, because they believed he was "double doctoring," said the judge.
